intro_html: Mongolian chicken has that sweet, garlicky, deeply savory sauce that makes rice disappear fast. The slow cooker version gives you all of it with 63 grams of protein per bowl for around $4.05 a serving (at everyday cost). One batch is 14 servings, so you're set for lunches and dinners without touching a restaurant menu.
cost_closing_html: About $4.05 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each bowl carries 63 grams of protein and just 564 calories, a genuinely lean, high-protein plate.
upsell_html: This one tastes like a splurge and cooks like a nap, which is exactly the deal we want. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Sesame oil looks pricey per bottle, but you use a splash, so one bottle lasts most of a year and pennies out per meal.
Brown sugar and soy sauce are pantry cheap, so keep them stocked and this sauce comes together on autopilot.
Frozen broccoli beats fresh on both price and shelf life, so reach for the freezer bag and stop losing crowns to the crisper drawer.
make_it: Combine the chicken, soy sauce, brown sugar, hoisin, sesame oil, and garlic in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken shreds with almost no effort.
Stir in the broccoli florets during the final 30 minutes so they cook through but stay green.
If you want a thicker sauce, spoon a little off, whisk in a pinch of cornstarch, and stir it back in.
Pull the chicken apart in the pot and serve over steaming white rice.
